long_biography.plain_text:
Swiss businessman Wenzel Gelpke financed the restoration of Villa Gelpke in Waldenburg between 2002 and 2004. Built for his ancestor, industrialist Gedeon Thommen, the house had suffered serious settlement and cracking. A conservation specialist assessed its importance before architects Steinmann and Rey undertook the repairs.

The project combined structural work with the recovery of historic finishes. Original oak windows, their fittings and handmade glass were retained, while paint investigation guided the reinstatement of earlier colours. In one room, red walls and black window frames were restored around a black marble fireplace. The associated historic outbuilding was also rehabilitated.
